description: The line plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and accuracy for three different measures—Final Accuracy, Δ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy—across a range of initial confidence values from 0.91 to 0.99. The x-axis, labeled "Initial Confidence," is a linear scale with tick marks at intervals of 0.01, ranging from 0.91 to 0.99. The y-axis, labeled "Accuracy," is also a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, with major gridlines at 0.2 intervals. The "Final Accuracy" (blue line with square markers) starts at approximately 0.85 when initial confidence is 0.91, rises to a peak of about 0.95 at an initial confidence of 0.93, and then gradually declines to around 0.88 at 0.99. The "Δ Accuracy" (orange line with diamond markers) begins at approximately 0.55, peaks at 0.7 at an initial confidence of 0.92, and then shows a general downward trend, ending at about 0.2 at 0.99. The "Initial Accuracy" (green line with circular markers) starts at around 0.4, dips to about 0.3 at 0.92, rises to a peak of approximately 0.85 at 0.98, and then decreases to about 0.75 at 0.99. Error bars are present for all data points, indicating variability in the measurements.
